```{r setup}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(readr); library(dplyr); library(knitr); library(tibble); library(stringr) })
OUT <- file.path("..", "output")
FIG <- function(file, width = "90%") {
  p <- file.path(OUT, "figures", file)
  if (file.exists(p))
    cat(sprintf("![](%s){fig-align=\"center\" width=%s}\n", p, width))
  else
    cat("::: {.placeholder}\n<span class='ph-tag'>\u25a2 pending data</span><br>Figure pending: run the corresponding script (see README) to generate it.\n:::\n")
}
.rdc <- function(p) tryCatch(readr::read_csv(file.path(OUT, p), show_col_types = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
.hd <- .rdc("tables/lfs_headlines.csv")
H <- function(k, d = 0) { if (is.null(.hd)) return("n/a"); v <- .hd$value[.hd$key == k]
  if (!length(v) || is.na(v[1])) "n/a" else formatC(v[1], format = "f", digits = d) }
.hh <- .rdc("tables/hsess_headlines.csv")
GAP <- function(k) { if (is.null(.hh)) return("n/a"); v <- .hh$value[.hh$key == k]
  if (!length(v) || is.na(v[1])) return("n/a"); sprintf("%.0f%% %s", abs(v[1]), ifelse(v[1] >= 0, "below", "above")) }
HS <- function(k, d = 0) { if (is.null(.hh)) return("n/a"); v <- .hh$value[.hh$key == k]
  if (!length(v) || is.na(v[1])) "n/a" else formatC(v[1], format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",") }
.kv <- .rdc("inventory/key_variables.csv")
.tests <- .rdc("models/lfs_tests.csv")
.htests <- .rdc("models/hsess_tests.csv")
ptab <- function(t) t %>% mutate(p = ifelse(p < .001, "<0.001", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 3)))
```

# 1 · Data and variables {.section-divider background-color="#00377C"}

## Data sources {.smaller}

- **SSSU Labour Force Survey 2021** (anonymised public-use file): 265.6k interviews from 151.7k persons aged 15+ in 88.1k households; rotation panel; collected before February 2022. Age is released in bands (15–24, 25–29 and older); the file has no earnings, household composition, displacement or disability variables.
- **UNICEF Household Social and Economic Status Survey (HSESS)**, December 2023 to February 2024, Institute of Demography and Quality of Life Problems: 18,838 individuals in 8,024 households, all regions except the occupied territories and Luhansk oblast. Single-year age; employment questions from age 15; displacement, disability (household level), childcare, earnings and household income.
- **MICS-7 2025/26**: access pending.

## Age groups {.smaller}

::: {.vmid-s}
::: {.tight-table}
| Age group | Indicators | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **15–18** | Education, training, NEET | Ages 14–17 are legal minors; HSESS asks employment questions from age 15 |
| **19–24** | Labour-force participation, employment, job quality, earnings, NEET | |
| **15–24** | Education-to-work transition, NEET | UNICEF programme age range |
| **15–29** | NEET | ILO age range for NEET, shown for reference |
:::
:::

::: {style="font-size:0.58em; color:#7a7a7a;"}
The LFS 2021 public file releases age in bands, so LFS results are shown for 15–24 (and 15–29 for NEET). The 15–18 and 19–24 groups use HSESS 2023/24, and MICS-7 once available.
:::

## Variables and definitions {.smaller}

::: {.tight-table}
| Concept | Definition | LFS 2021 |
|---|---|---|
| **Labour-force participation** | Employed or unemployed (ILO) | `labour_force` 1–2 |
| **Employed** | Worked at least one hour for pay or profit in the reference week, or temporarily absent | `labour_force` = 1 |
| **Unemployment rate** | Unemployed (no work, searched in last 4 weeks, available) as share of the labour force | `labour_force` = 2 |
| **NEET** | Not employed and not in education. In the LFS public file, unemployed students cannot be identified, so the LFS rate is an upper bound | `labour_force`, `reason_inactiv` |
| **Care burden (proxy)** | Outside the labour force because of home or family duties | `reason_inactiv` = 3 |
| **Informal employment** | No social contributions, no paid leave or sick leave, or oral agreement | `informal_empl` = 1 |
| **Short hours** | Under 30 hours actually worked in the reference week | `actual_duration` 1–2 |
| **Occupational segregation** | Dissimilarity index: share of women (or men) who would have to change occupation for equal distributions | `occupation` (9 groups) |
:::

::: {style="font-size:0.55em; color:#7a7a7a;"}
HSESS uses the same definitions: employment from IND_B1 (production for own household use only is not counted as employment), education from IND_A9, and labour-force participation as employed or looking for work or starting a business (IND_B21).
:::

# 4 · Regression analysis {.section-divider background-color="#00377C"}

## Linear probability models: NEET and labour-force participation, 15–24 (LFS 2021) {.smaller}
```{r f8, results='asis'}
FIG("f8_coefficients_en.png", "78%")
```

::: {style="font-size:0.58em; color:#7a7a7a;"}
Oblast fixed effects, weighted, standard errors clustered by person. Interaction terms show how the difference between women and men varies with marital status, area and higher education. Associations, not causal effects.
:::

# 5 · Next steps {.section-divider background-color="#00377C"}

## Points for discussion {.smaller .bigtitle}

::: {.vmid}
::: {.kf-list style="font-size:.84em;"}
**1. Age groups:** 15–18 and 19–24, with 15–24 and 15–29 for NEET.

**2. Sectors** to cover in the analysis of occupations: reconstruction, technical and digital, energy, manufacturing, green and care.

**3. Frontline oblasts** used for the regional breakdown.

**4. Data:** MICS-7 2025/26 microdata, SSSU wage statistics by occupation and sex, and public expenditure on skills, employment services and childcare.
:::
:::

## Next analyses {.smaller .bigtitle}

::: {.vmid}
::: {.kf-list style="font-size:.84em;"}
**Regressions:** contribution of childcare, displacement, disability, income and location to NEET, separately for 15–18 and 19–24; the same models on MICS-7 once available.

**Cost of inaction:** forgone earnings, output and fiscal revenue associated with differences in participation and NEET, using the benefit-cost framework of *A Brighter Future* (2024).

**Occupations:** check the self-reported occupation groups against the reported job titles, in particular the shares of women among machine operators and managers.

**Private sector:** costs and returns for employers of internships and apprenticeships combined with childcare support.
:::
:::

# Appendix {.section-divider background-color="#00377C"}

## HSESS variables used {.smaller}

::: {.kv-small}
```{r hvars}
hv <- .rdc("tables/hsess_variables_used.csv")
if (!is.null(hv)) {
  hv <- hv %>% filter(!is.na(code)) %>%
    mutate(code = case_when(role == "key" ~ "questionnaire key", role == "weight" ~ "final weight",
                            grepl("[^ -~]", code) ~ role, TRUE ~ code),
           v = paste0(role, " (", ifelse(file == "individual", "ind", "hh"), ")"))
  k <- ceiling(nrow(hv) / 3); pad <- function(x) c(x, rep("", 3 * k - length(x)))
  v <- pad(hv$v); cd <- pad(hv$code); i <- function(j) ((j - 1) * k + 1):(j * k)
  kable(data.frame(v[i(1)], cd[i(1)], v[i(2)], cd[i(2)], v[i(3)], cd[i(3)]), col.names = rep(c("Variable", "Code"), 3))
}
```
:::

::: {style="font-size:0.55em; color:#7a7a7a;"}
Codes as in the questionnaire and the "variables_ukr" sheet of each HSESS file; "ind" = individual file, "hh" = household file.
:::
